alex: Heads-up — I'm seeing a regression on 8xA100 pipeline runs after the kernel-selector tweak that went out last night. 1F1B throughput is ~9% lower, tail p99 latency up about 15ms on our 512-token validation set. Posting profiler excerpts below.

matt: Oof. Which model / microbatch config? Can you paste the top-line numbers?

alex: Model=gpt-xxl-8k (tp=2, pp=4), microbatch=2 (effective per-step batch=8), seq_len=512. Baseline commit abc123 -> current def456. Quick numbers from the load test:

```
baseline: 1200 infer/s, p99=42ms
current: 1092 infer/s, p99=57ms
delta: -9% throughput, +15ms p99
```

Profiling sketch (nvprof-style sampled):
```
[timeline] compute  65% -> 50%
[timeline] allreduce 15% -> 28%  (noticeable spike)
[timeline] idle/queue 5% -> 12%
Top kernels changed: ff_fwd_matmul_v2 (new) shows longer runtimes vs ff_fwd_matmul_v1 (old) for shape 4096x1024
```

priya: Interesting — I also saw KV cache eviction counts tick up on the same runs. Could be microbatching + kernel packing changes causing more frequent KV writes/reads. Run with --kv-debug to see evictions. Example log: `KVCache: evictions=124 -> 257` on current.

jing: @alex thanks for the numbers. The selector patch changed priority ordering to prefer newer fused kernels (ffn_v2, fused_gelu_v2). For our tensor shapes these fused kernels allocate slightly different workspace and can shift when we hit the continuous-batching threshold. That can reduce effective comm/compute overlap on PP.

matt: Do you have a minimal repro we can run locally? I'd like to capture NCCL traces.

alex: quick repro script I used (ran on staging cluster):
```bash
# repro-onef1b.sh
python run_pipeline.py --model gpt-xxl-8k --tp 2 --pp 4 --microbatch 2 --seq 512 --profile nvtx --commit def456
```
Then I pulled `/tmp/profiles/*.nvtx.json` and opened FlameScope. NCCL allreduce durations increased across the board.

deploy-bot: selector-change rollout finished to staging at 2024-06-24T02:12:09Z (deploy id: dpl-7823) :white_check_mark:

sara: Can we revert the selector change on staging to confirm it's the root cause before touching prod? I'd prefer a quick rollback + A/B run. :+1:

matt: I'll run an A/B with baseline abc123 vs def456 on the same node pool. Also will capture `nvprof --trace` and `nv-nsight` perf counters to quantify comm stall time.

alex: paste from a short nvprof snapshot (trimmed):
```
Kernel                          Time(ms)  Calls
ff_fwd_matmul_v2                3.8       512
ff_fwd_matmul_v1                2.4       1024
allreduce                        1.1 -> 2.6  (per-step increase)
queue_wait                       0.2 -> 0.9
```

priya: If the new kernel increases workspace, it may push microbatches into a different packing/comm pattern, which increases frequent small allreduces. We should check continuous-batching thresholds and `max_pack_tokens` config. Lowering `cb_threshold` from 32->16 sometimes restores overlap for these seq shapes.

jing: Another experiment: force the selector to prefer `ff_fwd_matmul_v1` for FFNs only (env override) and run the 1F1B test. If throughput recovers, we have a path: either adjust selector heuristics or add a shape-based exception. Example override: `KERNEL_SELECTOR_OVERRIDES='ffn:priority=v1'`

matt: Good plan. Also going to instrument per-stage timing to see which pipeline stage sees the biggest compute drop. Early signs point to stage 2 having more idle time post-change.

alex: I did a microbatch sweep (1..4) on the same commit, results:
```
microbatch=1 => 980 inf/s, p99=72ms
microbatch=2 => 1092 inf/s, p99=57ms
microbatch=3 => 1140 inf/s, p99=51ms  <- best here
microbatch=4 => 1130 inf/s, p99=53ms
```
So microbatch=3 restores most of the throughput but changes latency profile. That suggests the selector+packing interaction is sensitive to microbatch boundary alignment.

priya: OK — action items:
- matt: run A/B with NCCL traces + per-stage timing (ETA 2h)
- matt/jing: try selector override to v1 and microbatch=3 test (ETA 3h)
- alex: run KV-debug on repro and share eviction counts (done)
- sara: prepare rollback playbook for prod if we validate regression (ready)

jing: If experiments confirm, I'll open a patch to update selector heuristics to include shape-based cost model + a small regression test that runs 1F1B on a short validation corpus.

matt: Starting traces now. Will ping back with nvprof outputs.

alex: Thanks — the odd part is the allreduce jump. If the selector causes a small increase in per-layer kernel time, that can perturb the timing window and magnify allreduce cost across ranks. So we might be looking at a fragile timing interaction rather than a slow kernel alone.

sara: Keep me posted. If it's a fragility thing we should add a CI perf gate. :warning:

matt: update in 45m with traces.

alex: great — tagging @jing @priya so we can coordinate the quick fixes. :thumbsup:
